officialTitle: 21-Gene Assay to Inform Chemotherapy Benefit in Node-Positive Breast Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: A total of 5083 women (33.2% premenopausal and 66.8% postmenopausal) underwent randomization, and 5018 participated in the trial.
primaryEndpoints: Invasive disease-free survival; interaction with recurrence score
design.notes: Chemotherapy effect differed by menopausal status at the third interim analysis; separate prespecified analyses were reported for pre- and postmenopausal women.

clinicalQuestion: In HR+/HER2- breast cancer with 1-3 positive nodes and a 21-gene recurrence score of 25 or lower, does adding chemotherapy to endocrine therapy improve invasive disease-free survival?

pico.population: Women with HR+/HER2- breast cancer, 1-3 positive axillary nodes and a recurrence score of 25 or lower
pico.intervention: Chemotherapy followed by endocrine therapy (chemoendocrine therapy)
pico.outcomes: Primary: invasive disease-free survival and its interaction with recurrence score. Secondary: distant relapse-free survival

arms.label: Chemoendocrine therapy
arms.regimen: Adjuvant chemotherapy followed by endocrine therapy

publications.title: 21-Gene Assay to Inform Chemotherapy Benefit in Node-Positive Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Third prespecified interim analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Among postmenopausal women, invasive disease-free survival at 5 years was 91.9% in the endocrine-only group and 91.3% in the chemoendocrine group, with no chemotherapy benefit (hazard ratio for invasive disease recurrence, new primary cancer [breast cancer or another type], or death, 1.02; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.82 to 1.26; P = 0.89).

Among premenopausal women, invasive disease-free survival at 5 years was 89.0% with endocrine-only therapy and 93.9% with chemoendocrine therapy (hazard ratio, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43 to 0.83; P = 0.002), with a similar increase in distant relapse-free survival (hazard ratio, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.87; P = 0.009).

Among premenopausal women, invasive disease-free survival at 5 years was 89.0% with endocrine-only therapy and 93.9% with chemoendocrine therapy (hazard ratio, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43 to 0.83; P = 0.002), with a similar increase in distant relapse-free survival (hazard ratio, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.87; P = 0.009).

strengths: Large randomised trial addressing a common clinical scenario (node-positive, lower genomic risk)
limitations: Mechanism of premenopausal benefit (chemotherapy-induced ovarian suppression versus cytotoxic effect) not resolved by the design

clinicalImplications.text: Supports omission of adjuvant chemotherapy in postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2- breast cancer, 1-3 positive nodes and a recurrence score of 25 or lower, whereas premenopausal women in the same setting derived invasive disease-free survival benefit from chemoendocrine therapy.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Menopausal status, not the recurrence score itself, separated benefit in this trial — the relative chemotherapy benefit did not increase as the score increased.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 34914339. Later updated analyses not yet ingested.
